correctness.rationale: Writing R_n(w)=w(w+1)···(w+n−1), the two-block coefficient 2^{j−1}−1 converts the unnormalized PGF into (R_n(2z)−2R_n(z))/2, with zero constant and linear coefficients. Evaluation at 1 gives n!(n−1)/2, and factoring the first rising-factorial term yields 2z times the difference of the products over h=1,…,n−1 in the normalized formula. For each h and nonzero z with Re z≥0, the squared-modulus difference of 2z+h and z+h is 3|z|²+2h Re z>0. The second factor z+h is nonzero there, and the index set is nonempty for n≥2, so strict factorwise dominance implies the products cannot be equal, including on the imaginary axis. The z² coefficient is the positive unsigned Stirling number [n,2] divided by L(n,2); n=2 gives P=z². I independently multiplied the n=8 factors and compared to the rising-factorial coefficients and recomputed the cubic discriminant −307921820 and Routh margin 2301540. That confirms the exact nonreal example, not all-degree stability, which follows from the modulus proof. value.rationale: Two blocks are the first natural case beyond a single rising factorial; the family contains genuinely nonreal roots. The proof settles a cited conjectural location uniformly in n for that subfamily and explains why the imaginary axis is strictly excluded after factoring out zero. This is materially stronger than the finite sample or the trivial origin check.
